correctness.rationale: Both quartic gradients have no simultaneous projective zero. For every line z=sx+ty direct binary-quartic coefficient matching yields exact parameter equations; the complementary chart has only y=0. Factorization and finite-field trace-zero arguments show all 27 nonvertical lines on each curve split over F27/F81. The first contact quadratic has discriminant -1, hence two distinct degree-two contacts per line over the odd-degree line fields; the second is a linear-square, hence a fourfold contact. Unique tangent per smooth point ensures nonoverlap. The resulting orbit structures are 1^1 2^9 6^6 and 1^4 4^6. The pure-Python finite checker matches counts and cycles. No finite census is used as proof of infinite-field completeness.

originality.rationale: The full claim concerns the even-contact support and geometric Frobenius of all contact points on the two named characteristic-three quartics. Existing source equations, correspondence, and Galois/Weyl data can determine line and exceptional-component actions, but do not by themselves determine whether their ramification contact sections are one or two distinct points, or the contact-point orbit profile. The Hermitian hyperflex portion is a known comparison, and originality is located in the explicit paired classification and first quartic contact arithmetic; unresolved possible specialist historical tables are stated as a risk.
residual_risks: Undiscovered classical tables of characteristic-three quartic bitangents may reproduce the explicit first-curve contact arithmetic.
The second Hermitian-type curve has classical total hyperflex structure; this cannot be regarded as independently novel.
Abstract line and exceptional-curve Frobenius profiles can already be implied by prior Weyl-action computations; they are ancillary, not the main novelty claim.

value.rationale: These two naturally distinguished exceptional rational-point-minimal degree-two del Pezzo surfaces have intrinsic anticanonical branch quartics; multiplicities and Frobenius of their tangency supports are meaningful natural geometric/arithmetic invariants, not implied solely by rational point counts or Weyl actions. The complete contrast between ordinary and hyperflex contact schemes and sharp contact splitting fields is useful for studying arithmetic branch geometry. Scope does not rely on a speculative downstream theorem.
